chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Reconciliation is permissible between the people.
ai.seo_question: Is reconciliation permissible in Islamic law according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes reconciliation (sulh) as a universally permissible act, serving as a foundational legal principle in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes amicably. It underscores the high spiritual and social value of peace-making, often cited alongside the concept of 'goodness' (husn) in Islamic ethics. This principle allows parties to settle conflicts, including financial and marital matters, through mutual agreement rather than strict adjudication.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The reconciliation is permitted between the people’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Settlement by means of mutual agreement is permissible for people.’”
